name: Frankenstein (1818)
summary: A Gothic storm laboratory where lightning feeds the spark of life.
description: From the Sci-Fi 360 journey: an Alpine gorge in a thunderstorm, a stone viaduct, a galvanic coil tower and the creature on his lightning-rod platform.
learningObjectives: Discuss responsibility for new technology through Mary Shelley's novel.

display.title: FRANKENSTEIN
display.author: MARY SHELLEY
display.themeLine: Humanity tries to create life, and must answer for what it has made.

hotspots.label: Galvanic coil
hotspots.title: The spark of life
hotspots.text: Galvanism, using electricity to make muscles twitch, helped inspire the idea that a spark might bring life.

facts.text: Published anonymously in London on 1 January 1818.

hotspots.archive: They thought lightning might hold the spark of life.

hotspots.label: The creature
hotspots.title: The creature
hotspots.text: Victor Frankenstein never names his creation; the novel calls it the creature. It reaches out, and Victor runs from what he made.
hotspots.archive: He never asked to be made.

question.why: Victor makes life, then abandons it; the story asks what creators owe their creations.

hotspots.archive: A story begun on a stormy summer night.

facts.text: Published anonymously in London on 1 January 1818.
Mary Shelley began the story at 18, in a ghost-story contest at Lake Geneva in 1816.
Victor Frankenstein never names his creation. The novel calls it the creature.
Galvanism, using electricity to make muscles twitch, helped inspire the idea of a spark of life.
The subtitle compares Victor to Prometheus, who stole fire from the gods.
